messages.subject: is it possible to simulate connected crosses ?
messages.subject_clean: is it possible to simulate connected crosses ?
messages.body_plain:
Dear Karl,
I want to simulate genetic data files for connected crosses (with parents common to some crosses; in my case, a half-diallel) to compare different strategies to obtain an integrated map. As I understand, sim.cross can simulate genetic data only for a single cross. Do you think that there would be any possibility to use it also to obtain simulated genetic data for connected crosses ?
Thank you in advance for your answer.
Agnes Doligez

messages.body_plain:
We are using Rqtl for trait association in RIL melon populations.

Recently, we have started using the two-QTL scans for analysing our data and predicting potential interactions.

I use the package for creating a twoscan object. When plotting it seems the plot image is a matrix of the lod score for all markersXmarkers. When I use summary, each chromosome combinations is represented by a single line.

My question is whether a matrix for markerXmarker lod score (considering each lod type for each model, e.g., full, additive) exists and how can I have access to these values?

messages.body_plain:
As described in the "Value" section of the help file for scantwo, the output of scantwo is a list with three components. The first component is a matrix of dimension [tot.pos x tot.pos]; the upper triangle contains the LOD scores for the additive model, and the lower triangle contains the LOD scores for the full model. The diagonal contains the results of scanone <http://127.0.0.1:24822/library/qtl/help/scanone>.

karl

messages.body_plain:
I think you want n.marcovar to be equal to the number of detectable QTL. But this is not something that you'd know in advance, and in my mind it's the main disadvantage of this sort of CIM approach and why I prefer the penalized LOD score criterion encompassed in stepwiseqtl(). See Broman and Speed (2002) https://www.biostat.wisc.edu/~kbroman/publications/jrssb.pdf

But for sure you'll want to re-do the permutations for the chosen value of n.marcovar, but this won't account for the search over different values of n.marcovar, if you're going to try different values and then pick the strongest results.

karl

messages.body_plain:
R/qtl is designed for diploid organisms, and for crosses between inbred lines. In an F2 intercross between two inbred strains, the offspring would have genotype AA, AB, or BB, with the parents being A and B.

>From SNP genotypes, parents would be either 0 or 2 and offspring 0, 1, or 2. You’d take all SNPs where A parent is 0 and B parent is 2 and recode the offspring as 0 → AA, 1 → AB, 2 → BB. For SNPs where A parent is 2 and B parent is 0, you’d recode the offspring as 0 → BB, 1 → AB, 2 → AA.

In the case of outbred parents, you also have cases where one or the other parent is heterozygous. And to handle these in R/qtl you also need to have inferred phase. Really, R/qtl doesn’t quite have the facilities for doing map construction in an outbred F2.

With tetraploids, don’t you need dosages at the SNPs? It’s not just 0,1,2.

karl

messages.body_plain:
Hi!
I hope it's not against the rules to ask two questions in one post!

The first question that I have is how to structure a very large data set for use in r/qtl. I've got RAD data with so many loci that I can't edit the data in Excel. This has presented a problem because, despite my best efforts, r/qtl doesn't want to recognize my "chromosome" line when there are two fields with "NA" in them. When I've tried with a smaller data set in excel, deleting "NA" and saving it as a csv works just fine. The process that I'm using to create the read.cross data set is by assembling it from a .vcf output. This is in the format ".012", which means that I get two files that I'm combining: 1) a file with all of the loci and the number of "reference alleles" at each (0 = BB, 1 = BA, 2 = AA) 2) a file with all of the individual identifiers. I'm gluing these files together in R, but to insert the line that has "chromosome number" on it (I'm calling them all chromosome 1 since I don't have that information yet), I have to create a list that contains the blank cells, as described in the tutorial.

I've used this code to do this:
> chromosome <- c(NA,NA,rep(1,43975)) where 43975 is the number of loci

Then glue this to the top, producing the attached file. When I run read.cross, I get the following error:
> sample_cross <- read.cross(file = "small_matrix.csv", format = 'csv', na.strings = c("-1", "NA"),  genotypes = c("0", "1", "2"), alleles = c("A", "B"))

Error in read.cross.csv(dir, file, na.strings, genotypes, estimate.map,  :
You must include at least one phenotype (e.g., an index). There was this value in the first column of the second row 'NA' where was supposed to be nothing.

My second question is about study design. My data (155 individuals) are spread across a number of crosses, some backcross and some intercross. I'm thinking that I should be analyzing them separately (at least by type, but they have different parents, so maybe also by brood?), but I haven't seen much in the literature on what to do with multiple families. Any suggestions, or could you point me towards resources for this problem? To be clear, I'm working with only one phenotype, but multiple lines of crosses from (non-model system) wild-caught individuals.
Thank you so much for your time, and for the software!

Best,
Evan
